title: Handoff gap analysis and afternoon signal slate
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc to capture gaps in our current handoff flow and a compact ‘afternoon signal slate’ — a minimal set of checks and calendar entries for the mid-day -> nightshift transition during releases. Narrow focus: portability gaps (who knows what), telemetry blind spots, and a terse release-notes draft we can iterate on with PM/Comms.

Background/context:
- Last two soft-launches had ambiguous ownership of the canary rollback step between 18:00-22:00 PT. We saw delayed rollbacks and some noisy alerts that weren’t properly triaged.
- Current runbooks (see RLSE-4123) list a long checklist; ops teams want a shorter signal set for handoffs.
- This doc sits between the full preflight runbook and the operator pocket guide — purposely lightweight.

Summary of identified gaps (quick):
- Missing single-source-of-truth for who is the day->evening handoff owner (no roster link in the runbook).
- Telemetry: prefix/KV cache error rates aren’t shown on the short dashboard used by on-call (thresholds undefined).
- Rollback comms: no canned Slack alert template for immediate rollback (we currently type freeform).
- Release notes: no short user-facing change summary in the ops release digest (PMs push longer writeups late).
- Capacity throttle knobs: dedicated/autoscale fallback thresholds absent from the evening runbook.

Afternoon signal slate (one-page operational checklist — read during handoff):
1) Ownership and communication
   - Confirm handoff owner and backup in Slack (#deploy-ops). Owner must explicitly post: "I accept handoff: NAME (timezone) — monitoring + rollback owner".
   - Post short release note to #deploy-ops with link to release-notes draft and canary % in telemetry.
2) Canary/traffic checks (first 30m)
   - Canary throughput within expected band? (compare to baseline sparkline).
   - Error-rate: 5xx spike > 3x baseline -> escalate to SRE lead.
   - Latency p95 increase > 30% -> consider traffic throttle to 50%.
3) Telemetry sanity (quick probes)
   - KV cache hit-rate not below 85% for any model serving node.
   - Prefix cache size growth: sustained linear increase > 10%/10m -> tag for investigation.
   - Tokens/sec per-GPU within expected curve; check m/gpu-token metric.
4) Rollback readiness (confirm)
   - Confirm rollback plan is posted and validated for current build (PR link).
   - Confirm fallback model variant/region is available and warmed.
5) Post-release user-facing checks (15m after landing)
   - Smoke queries (3 prompts): basic generation + function-call scenario + embeddings sanity.
   - Docs/Changelogs: short bullet summary present in release-notes draft.
6) Nightwatch notes for on-call
   - If threshold X breached -> escalate to on-call SRE and product on-call. Template: "[IMMEDIATE] Release {version} - {metric} breached - action: rollback?"
   - If noisy alerts on model routing -> switch traffic to fallback variant and open incident channel.

Timeline / compact rollout calendar (72h view — example for this patch):
- T-48h: Feature freeze + security signoff (docs link: RLSE-4123).
- T-24h: Preflight ticket review + operator checklist completion.
- Day 0 10:00 PT: Dry-run in staging (smoke + perf).
- Day 0 14:00 PT: Canary deploy (5% traffic). 0–30m observe, then 30–120m ramp.
- Day 0 18:00 PT: Full rollout decision window (ops capture decision in #deploy-ops).
- Day 1 09:00 PT: Stability review + telemetry deep-dive (if stable, close watch).

Who needs to be pinged (short list):
- SRE lead: Marco Ruiz (pager + Slack).
- Serving runtime eng: Evelyn Zhang (debugging/model fallback).
- Product/PM: Noah Brooks (user-facing changes / rollback signoff).

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Create a canned Slack rollback template and add to the runbook — owner: Aisha — due: 2025-09-14.
- Add roster link to the handoff section + automated daily reminder for the handoff owner — owner: Marco — due: 2025-09-16.
- Add concise release-summary slot to the PM checklist (1–2 sentences) — owner: Noah — due: 2025-09-13.
- Add KV/prefix cache quick panels to the operator pocket dashboard — owner: Evelyn — due: 2025-09-20.

Release notes (ops-first draft — send to PM for copy-edit):
Title: 2025.09.10 - Serving runtime: adaptive-batching + small model fallback adjustments
Short summary (2 lines): Improved steady-state throughput for short sequences and added a fallback routing variant to reduce tail latency in high-load conditions. No breaking changes to API.
User-facing bullets:
- Reduced median latency on short sequences by ~12% in low-load tests.
- New fallback model variant will be transparently routed during autoscale events to preserve availability; customers on Dedicated can opt-out.
- Minor update to token pricing telemetry (internal only — billing unaffected).
Known issues / risk notes:
- Rarely observed transient higher latencies during aggressive prefix-caching warmup (observed in staging runs). Ops will monitor and revert if p95 > 2x baseline in first 60m.
- Canary might surface higher embedding variance for models > 4k tokens; PM investigating evaluation set.

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Do we want the handoff owner assert-statement automated (bot post) or manual? (cost/time tradeoff).
- Is the PM comfortable with the short two-line release summary — need signoff from Comms.
- Should Dedicated customers receive an opt-in email when fallback routing is enabled? (legal / billing check).

Quick links:
- Full preflight runbook: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RE/Preflight+Checklist
- Canary telemetry dashboard: grafana.redwood.ai/d/ciYv/canary-slate
- RLSE Jira epic: RLSE-4123
- PR for adaptive batching changes: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2841

Notes to self:
- This is intentionally terse; aim to fold into the main runbook after owners close action items.
- After first nightwatch, capture a 6-line postmortem if any manual intervention required.

-- Aisha (ops)
